summary.name: Encyclopedia of Agentic Coding Patterns
summary.one_liner: A free online pattern language of 300+ patterns, antipatterns, and concepts for building software with AI agents, from product judgment to agentic construction.
keywords: how to build software with ai
use_cases: learning how to direct AI agents through software work
deciding what product to build before coding
reviewing governance and approval policies for agents
understanding agent security and prompt injection risks
designing software architecture for agent-friendly codebases
summary.what_it_does: The book organizes its entries into 14 sections, from strategic topics like product judgment and intent/scope to tactical topics like testing, security, operations, and socio-technical systems. Each pattern is self-contained and follows a consistent format with Context, Problem, and other fields, so readers can read in any order. The largest section, Agentic Software Construction, covers agents, tools, MCP, subagents, skills, prompts, and context engineering. A separate section on Agent Governance and Feedback covers approval policies, evals, human-in-the-loop, and bounded autonomy. It is described as an encyclopedia rather than a tutorial.
notable: 300+ patterns, antipatterns, and concepts organized into 14 sections
Each entry follows a consistent pattern-language format
Largest section covers agentic software construction (72 entries)
caveats: Described as an encyclopedia, not a tutorial
Page text does not state a license or formal pricing details beyond it being freely available per the listing
